comparison: Perfect agreement on claims C25-C37. Both evaluations find the CRISPRi/a and ChIP-qPCR evidence for E9 enhancer function compelling and supported. OpenEval emphasizes bidirectional effects and specificity; peer reviewers explicitly validate the functional identification and histone mark documentation.

Strong agreement on allele-specific effects (C38-C48). Both find evidence from reporter assays, CRISPR models, and human liver specimens compelling. OpenEval result includes C38 not mentioned by peer reviewers, but peer reviewers include broader claims C3, C5, C56 connecting to overall model. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Agreement on allele-specific expression in human tissues (C49-C56 overlap on C51-C55). Both find the approach valid and the human tissue data strengthens confidence. OpenEval notes technical sophistication and acknowledges imperfect LD as introducing uncertainty; peer reviewers emphasize this validates the cell line findings.

Disagreement on chromatin interaction evidence (C57, C58, C81). OpenEval finds 3C-qPCR data provides 'direct evidence for enhancer-promoter looping' and rates SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, noting the data is 'consistent with' but may not 'directly demonstrate' promoter-enhancer interactions, suggesting higher standards for this claim.

Perfect agreement on 5-FU sensitivity data (C6, C59, C60). Both find the >10-fold IC50 difference compelling and functionally links variant to drug response. OpenEval emphasizes statistical significance and dose-dependent relationship; peer reviewers note this provides confidence in proposed mechanisms.

Strong agreement on CEBPB mechanism (C62-C68, C82-C83). Both find convergence of computational, functional, and biochemical evidence compelling. OpenEval notes C61 and acknowledges contradiction with in silico predictions (C102); peer reviewers focus on the multiple lines of evidence supporting CEBPB recruitment. Both rate SUPPORTED.

Perfect agreement on CEBPB knockdown experiments (C69-C72). Both find the genotype-specific loss-of-function evidence compelling for establishing causal link between variant, CEBPB binding, and functional outcomes. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Perfect agreement on population genetics data (C73-C75, C89-C90). Both accept the gnomAD allele frequency data and carrier frequency calculations. Peer reviewers explicitly note the high compromised allele frequency supports broader significance of findings. Both rate SUPPORTED.

Partial overlap on main findings summary (C3, C5, C84, C85). OpenEval groups these with C84-C85 as appropriately cautious about biomarker designation. Peer reviewers include C3, C5 with allele-specific effects data (R2) and find overall model compelling. Both support the biological mechanism while acknowledging clinical validation is needed.

Agreement on speculative nature but different emphasis (C86, C93-C95). OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN, noting claims are explicitly speculative and lack clinical/tumor data. Peer reviewers rate SUPPORTED, accepting translational implications as 'valuable findings' while acknowledging tumor resistance remains somewhat speculative. Different thresholds for speculation.
OpenEval evaluates cancer health disparities background claims (C91, C92) as SUPPORTED with appropriate citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these contextual claims.

OpenEval evaluates acknowledgment of computational prediction discrepancy (C102-C104) as SUPPORTED, noting transparent reporting strengthens conclusions. No corresponding peer review evaluation, though peer R6 implicitly accepts CEBPB mechanism despite this contradiction.
OpenEval evaluates novelty claims (C105, C106, C108) as SUPPORTED with appropriate caveats. No corresponding peer review evaluation of these specific novelty assertions.
OpenEval evaluates contextualization with known DPYD variants (C112-C115) as SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation of these claims relating findings to prior pharmacogenetic knowledge.
OpenEval evaluates background/context claims (C1, C2, C11-C17) as SUPPORTED with appropriate citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation of these introductory claims.
OpenEval evaluates DPYD/5-FU background (C18-C24) as SUPPORTED with appropriate citations establishing clinical significance. No corresponding peer review evaluation of these background claims.
OpenEval evaluates 5-FU pharmacology discussion points (C76-C80) as SUPPORTED with appropriate citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation of these contextual discussion claims.

OpenEval evaluates CEBPB biology background (C96-C101) as SUPPORTED, noting C99 inference about active isoforms is reasonable despite lack of isoform-specific experiments. No corresponding peer review evaluation.
OpenEval evaluates discussion of connections to prior work (C107-C111) as SUPPORTED, noting appropriate speculation about dynamic therapy response. No corresponding peer review evaluation.

OpenEval rates claim C4 about 27% 'global' MAF as UNCERTAIN, noting this oversimplifies population-specific variation (7-40%) and lacks clear sourcing. No corresponding peer review evaluation of this specific claim.

OpenEval evaluates summary of human tissue validation (C87, C88) as SUPPORTED, noting consistency with prior work and validation of cell line findings. No corresponding peer review evaluation, though peer R3 addresses overlapping tissue validation claims.
OpenEval evaluates background on resistance mechanisms (C9, C10) as SUPPORTED with appropriate citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation of these motivational background claims.
